LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. The Bills have used a strong offensive attack to lead the way, with quarterback Josh Allen gunning for another MVP award. Allen's focus is on helping the Bills take home the Super Bowl trophy this year, and this entire team feels different this time around. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

Coming off a disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints continue to struggle with offensive consistency and finishing games under head coach Kellen Moore. Those problems could prove costly against a well-rounded Chicago team that boasts one of the NFL's most productive offenses and a top-10 defense. Can the Saints pull off an unlikely upset, or will their struggles continue against one of the NFC's top contenders? Here's how our staff predicts Sunday's matchup will unfold. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 28-14 This is a game that doesn’t favor the Saints. The Bears are by far the best team the Saints have faced since the Detroit Lions , who beat New Orleans in overtime. They have one of the league’s best offenses , led by quarterback Caleb Williams , and one of the league's most balanced teams. Defensively, the Bears have a top-10 defense. Chicago boasts a top-10 defense, ranking eighth in scoring (20.4 PPG) and seventh in total defense (310.9 YPG). Their strength lies against the run, allowing 91.1 yards per game (seventh-fewest), while placing 15th against the pass (219.8 YPG). Crucially, the Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense (22.8% conversion rate allowed) and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown efficiency (53.8%). They maintain consistent pass pressure with 26 sacks (ninth) and seven interceptions (tied for 11th). Also, this will be the first cold-weather game for the Saints as the temperature will be in the 50s throughout the game. I don’t think the Saints will pull off the upset, but what I do know is that the Saints have played better on the road as both of their wins came on the road against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants . I do think its defense will do enough to make this game tight before Chicago pulls away near the end. Prediction : Bears 28 Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: L 32-21 This is a Saints team that seems to be searching, searching for an identity, a consistent offense, people on the same page. The New Orleans offense sputters and coughs more than my old 1969 VW Beetle. No matter what I would do to that little air-cooled engine, it never could quite get started, and when it did, it usually took a few minutes of driving before it would get going smoothly. Once it was warmed up, that little thing was a joy to drive. Unfortunately, it took a while to even get to that point. The Saints O reminds me of that Beetle. They can't seem to get going in the beginning. Once they get warmed up and going, they are fun to watch. Until then, it's almost torturous to be a part of. Eventually, I had to get rid of that little car. Keeping the valves aligned properly on that rapidly expanding air-cooled engine proved to be one of those "I'll be doing this forever" kind of projects, so I just gave up and moved on. The New Orleans offense is at that point, in my opinion. A squad that cannot consistently move the ball, stopping and starting itself with poor run blocking, or wide receivers and a quarterback who aren't on the same page, or play calling that comes across as vanilla as can be (think runs in the middle). Now, Brandon Staley's group is another story, another car if you will. They remind me of a Tesla. The Saints defense can really get going with the first acceleration, but fade at the end. A battery-powered Tesla is a lot like that. They can fly right out the gate and tear the street up, but don't expect that to last, as those batteries won't go 300-plus miles (no matter what they say) like a gas-power engine will, losing energy much sooner than their gas counterparts. This Saints defense has produced through the first three quarters, especially for the last few games. Although getting turnovers has been a notable absence for this group, it has played well, up until the final quarter. To wit, the Panthers' game. I say all that to say this: you cannot do any of what the offense and defense has been doing against a quality team. The Panthers, Browns, and Steelers were not quality teams. This Bears team is. It will take a complete game, start to finish, for this Saints team to have a chance to beat Chicago. The local boys haven't done that all year long. Prediction : Bears 32 Saints 21 Saints Mailbag Wednesdays, On SI Saints will answer your questions about what we see from our vantage point. To submit your thoughts or inquiries click here . Wiltfong Jr. · SB Nation Sun, November 22, 2026 at 6:33 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Windy City Gridiron crew makes their pick and some predictions for the Chicago Bears vs. New Orleans Saints game. Sam Householder: I'm trying to recalibrate my expectations. I think the Bears are due for a blowout. Coming off the bye, heading into a tough stretch, they can't be caught in a look-ahead spot, and I don't think Ben will let them. This is the worst defense they've faced in a month and probably all season. Bears 38, Saints 14 Josh Sunderbruch: I think there's rust to shake off, and for about a quarter or two it looks closer than it should, followed by the Bears steadily pulling away. Final score: Bears 31, Saints 17, with backups playing the final drive. Mongo Peanut: The Bears come out of the bye on fire, with their running game tuned up for a playoff push. The Saints hit a couple of shots to Olave, but otherwise look lifeless after a letdown against Carolina. Bears 38, Saints 13. Jacob Infante: The Bears looked sloppier than expected against the Buccaneers, but they still found a way to win. That's the sign of a good team, and knowing Ben Johnson, he used this bye week to recalibrate and get the offense back on track. I trust Chicago to get out to an early lead and force the Saints to play from behind, where I can see Jeffery Simmons tallying two sacks for the afternoon. Bears 34, Saints 20 Gary Baugher Jr.: I have the Bears by at least two touchdowns this week; the ground game is going to get back on track, Caleb Williams will throw for 2+ TDs, and Tyler Shough will be sacked 4+ times. Shough to Olave deep has worked all season, so I expect them linking up a few times, but a lack of a ground game and identity on the OL and the defense as a whole for the Saints will make this a lopsided affair. Bears 38, Saints 17 (edited) Jeff Berckes: My colleagues are predicting offensive point totals in the 30s, and I say… why so conservative?! My colleagues are also allowing for the Saints to get into the end zone. Why so scared? Ben got a chance to get in the lab. Dennis Allen Revenge Game. I'll say Bears 70, Saints negative 3. TJ Starman: I think there's plenty of reason to expect fireworks on this game. While the Bears are firmly the better team, I wouldn't be surprised to see the Saints trade a few haymakers along the way (or even in garbage time) in a matchup more akin to Carolina/Atlanta than Tampa Bay. Bears win big, 41 – 24 Lester A. Wiltfong Jr.: I predicted Bears 38, Saints 17 earlier this week, so I'll stick with that. Even though Kyle Monangai is back, I think D'Andre Swift will have a big day, with 100+ yards on the ground and another touchdown. Caleb will get his too, with 3 passing TDs and over 300 total yards. GOOCH : Some national media has this as a Bears loss for no discernable reason. At least with the Bucs there was a top defense and some bad luck involved. I have the Bears giving the Saints a beating – Caleb throws for three touchdowns, that Guy adds a rushing TD in his return, and Burden, Loveland, and Rome add the recieving TDs. On defense the Bears stifle the Saints offense and force three turnovers with four sacks (Booker, Sweat, Simmons, Grady) against the hapless Saints offense. Santos adds two field goals to make it 34 – 6 as the Bears and the Pope refuse to answer the Saints prayers. Superfans: Not gonna lie… we came here to drop another stone-cold lead pipe; take it to the bank, lock of a prediction, but after seeing what JB put down, we just want to echo those sentiments. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions for New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears in Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football winners/losers Current wins 1st title Wemby drops 50 ... again Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates 4 Bold Predictions for New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears in Week 11 Neal Coolong · Athlon Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 6:06 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Soldier Field in late November isn't where a 3-6 team usually goes to turn its season around, but the New Orleans Saints are still one game behind Carolina in the NFC South. Carl Granderson and the Saints' pass rush get a 7-2 Chicago Bears team coming off its bye, with kickoff set for noon CT on FOX. New Orleans will be shorthanded up front. Center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga missed practice again Thursday, according to the Saints injury report , and Kellen Moore said Asim Richards will miss a few weeks with a knee injury. Here are four bold predictions for how the Saints pull the upset anyway. Carl Granderson and Chase Young combine for three sacks Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) reacts to a play against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Granderson has 8.5 sacks and Young has eight, and the two of them have carried the pass rush all season. Against Carolina, Granderson had seven pressures and Young had five, according to PFF . Set that next to what Chicago has allowed. Caleb Williams has been sacked 14 times in six games, while the Saints' two edge rushers have 16.5 sacks between them. Chicago's Super Bowl hopes depend on Williams staying upright. Three sacks between Granderson and Young keep this a low-scoring game, which is the only kind New Orleans can win. Saints hold the Bears under 100 rushing yards Oct 19, 2025; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) runs the ball against New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (33) and linebacker Pete Werner (20) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The Bears average 142 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift leads them with 576 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Kyle Monangai, a full participant this week after a toe injury, has averaged 5.4 yards per carry. New Orleans has been better against the run since its bye. Cleveland and Carolina combined for 192 yards on 66 carries, 2.9 per attempt, according to the Saints' team site . "From a big-picture perspective, felt like controlling their run game was important, I felt like we did that," Moore said Monday. Linebacker Pete Werner, who leads the team with 70 tackles, missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a hamstring injury, which makes this one bolder. Kaden Elliss had seven stops against Carolina, and he'll have to clean up the middle if Werner can't go. Jordyn Tyson catches his first NFL touchdown Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (0) dives for the sideline with Cleveland Browns cornerback Myles Harden (26) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn ImagesMatthew Hinton-Imagn Images The rookie has taken over Bryce Lance's snaps , and he has 15 catches for 110 yards in two games. When Carolina took away Chris Olave , Tyson became Tyler Shough's top target. He's still looking for his first touchdown, and he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with a chest injury. If he plays, the red zone is where it happens. New Orleans has scored touchdowns on 72.4% of its red-zone trips, and Chicago will spend plenty of attention on Olave. Saints intercept Caleb Williams twice Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (7) steals the ball and runs it in for a touchdown against Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton (13) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images New Orleans has four interceptions all season, which is what makes this one bold. Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. have two apiece, and Emerson missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a concussion. Williams has thrown five interceptions in six games, and Bears quarterbacks have nine as a team. Chicago is minus-4 in turnover margin and New Orleans is minus-8, according to the Saints' game preview . Some Bears fans already see a trap game here. Two takeaways spring it, and the Saints leave Chicago at 4-6 with a 23-20 win. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. That has led to chaos among the defensive coaching ranks. The Cowboys are at home for this week's game against the 1-8 Tennessee Titans, and are 7.5-point favorites according to our friends at FanDuel. The over/under is 54.5 points. Let's get into three bold predictions for the Titans game. Tony Pollard goes off Tony Pollard returns to his old home as one of the main cogs in the Titans offense. Pollard has 628 yards rushing this year with six rushing touchdowns, along with 136 yards receiving an an additional touchdown. Against Dallas, who has trouble containing running backs, especially dual-threat ones, Pollard will have a day. He will amass over 100 yards from scrimmage and will score twice. Mike Pettine's defense gets two turnovers and a score This is more hope than anything else. The Cowboys defense needs something good to happen, and this week the Titans will oblige. While struggling with Pollard, they will frustrate Cam Ward and the passing attack with pressure and tight coverage on the Titans' short passing game. Things will go so well that they will actually score a touchdown on defense. CeeDee Lamb is the star with over 150 yards recieving Last week, it was George Pickens who kept the Cowboys in the game against the 49ers. CeeDee Lamb came on late to help out, but spent much of the game on the wrong page with Dak Prescott. That gets smoothed out this week as Lamb goes off for over 150 yards receiving and a receiving touchdown. Ok, over to you. What is your one bold prediction for the game? picks.headline: Cowboys vs Titans: Writer predictions for Week 11
picks.blurb: Cowboys vs Titans: Writer predictions for Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football winners/losers Current wins 1st title Wemby drops 50 ... again Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Cowboys vs Titans: Writer predictions for Week 11 Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images | Getty Images Mike Poland · SB Nation Sat, November 21, 2026 at 10:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Dallas gets one of its best opportunities of the season to steady things after the 46-40 loss to San Francisco. Tennessee is 1-8 and ranks near the bottom of the league on both sides of the ball. Dallas should be the better team here, but after giving up 584 yards last week, the defense still has something to prove. When Tennessee has the ball Tennessee should lean heavily on Tony Pollard. The former Cowboy has 628 rushing yards and six touchdowns, and Dallas has just been gashed for 214 yards on the ground by San Francisco. If the Titans can get Pollard moving early, it takes pressure off Cam Ward and gives Tennessee a chance to control the tempo. Dallas has to make Ward win this game through the air. Tennessee ranks near the bottom of the league in scoring and total offense, while Ward has been inconsistent despite showing flashes. The Cowboys need to contain Pollard, keep Ward in the pocket and force long third downs. With Tennessee also dealing with injuries at receiver, Dallas should have the advantage if it avoids the missed tackles and busted assignments that hurt so badly last week. When Dallas has the ball This is where Dallas should take control. Tennessee owns the league's worst pass defense, while Dak Prescott is playing some of his best football and just threw five touchdowns against San Francisco. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both capable of taking over a game, Dallas should attack downfield rather than becoming too conservative. Javonte Williams still needs enough work to keep Tennessee honest, but this matchup belongs in Prescott's hands. The Titans can create turnovers, so Dallas cannot get careless, but if the offensive line protects well there should be favourable matchups across the field all afternoon. The Cowboys should have too much firepower for Tennessee. If Dallas tackles better, limits Pollard and avoids gifting the Titans short fields, this is a game it should control. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (5-5) Often a shakeup mid-season sees at least a temporary improvement in performance. I think that will be the case here. Cowboys 34 Titans 23 Brandon Loree (7-3) The Cowboys made a big shakeup this week by taking play-calling duties away from Christian Parker. I feel like the defense is going to try to win this game for their defensive coordinator, and it sets them up well with the Tennessee Titans coming to town. The Titans should be a get-right game for the Cowboys on all fronts, for a team that's in desperate need of a win. Dallas should have their best performance of the season on defense and should have a strong performance on offense, leading to a 34-17 win before Thanksgiving. Dyllan Rivers (6-4) The Cowboys have struggled against every team this season, good and bad. Considering the game day changes Dallas has made with the defensive play-calling duties, there is a chance Dallas finally takes care of things against a bad team early in a game instead of in the waning moments. But I won't trust it until I see it. My gut feeling tells me Dallas wins by a touchdown or less. Let's go with 31-27 Cowboys Matt Holleran (5-5) The Cowboys are no doubt a mess, but this absolutely has to be a get-right matchup for them. With all the issues both on and off the field I don't have much confidence they'll do it, but I'm going to pick Dallas to get a win. Give me the Cowboys, 33-23. Mike Poland (4-6) To lose this one would bring shame to the game for Dallas. Sure, things are rough right now for the Cowboys after last week, and to lose this one would be a massive shock to all of Cowboys Nation. Confidence is best described as positive, but skidish. Cowboys win 31-17.

picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On Sunday, the Detroit Lions could be facing a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team devoid of two of its top players: QB Baker Mayfield (foot injury) and S Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle). Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 campaign with more interceptions (four) than passing touchdowns (three). However, he's still a better option under center than undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who took first-team reps in practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers. Daniels, who has already started three games this season due to injury issues for Mayfield, has also thrown for more interceptions (five) than touchdowns (three). Tampa Bay subsequently has not been very proficient through the air this season. In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six). Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players. A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties. Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. As for the Lions, they will be down two of their defensive captains and very best players in Week 11: LB Jack Campbell (neck) and EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL). Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026. Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue. Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers. Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule. The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury. As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7? Caleb Skinner, Writer: Lions 20, Bucs 17 It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions. The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down. While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay. The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year. Overall Record: 5-4 James Hill, Writer: Lions 24, Bucs 17 Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done. Overall Record: 4-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Lions 27, Bucs 21 As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not. Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years. For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore. Overall Record: 6-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Lions 27, Bucs 20 Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack. That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers. River Wells, Editor: Lions 24, Bucs 16 The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions. The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season. Consensus: Lions 5, Bucs 0 Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here. It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't. Tampa Bay has scored touchdowns on 15 of its 31 trips inside the 20 and settled for field goals on 12 others. That's why this ends with Chase McLaughlin. He's made all 22 of his field-goal attempts this season, and a close game in Detroit finally breaks Tampa Bay's way on his leg. Bucs 23, Lions 21. away.headline: Buccaneers May Need Rookie QB Jalon Daniels at the Worst Time
away.blurb: Mayfield’s availability remains the central variable. If he can return, the Buccaneers gain their veteran starter for an important NFC road test. If he cannot, Daniels’ legs, decision-making, and ability to avoid costly possessions will determine whether Tampa Bay can make its rushing attack the centerpiece of a credible upset bid. – The Lions placed linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) on injured reserve, while edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is out for the season. Those absences could make Daniels’ scrambling ability and Tampa Bay’s ground game more consequential if the rookie starts. Buccaneers’ Keionte Scott Earns Rookie Recognition, but One Flaw Stands Out Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (leg) has an uncertain outlook for Sunday’s (Nov. 22) road game against the Detroit Lions, creating the possibility rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make another start. The Buccaneers need Mayfield’s status clarified quickly because Daniels’ mobility could change the offense’s approach in a matchup expected to hinge on controlling possession, protecting the football, and keeping Detroit’s high-powered attack off the field. Locked On Bucs host James Yarcho said Daniels took the first-team reps after Mayfield missed Wednesday’s practice. The official team preview also listed Mayfield’s lower-leg injury as a major question for the week and noted Tampa Bay promoted Easton Stick from the practice squad, underscoring the need for quarterback insurance. Daniels has started three games while Mayfield was sidelined. He has supplied a dimension the offense can use if he starts again. He has rushed 22 times for 123 yards, a 5.6-yard average, while completing 60 of 98 passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions. Yarcho does not suggest Daniels is the more polished passer, but rather his ability to escape the pocket could extend drives against a Lions defense missing key front-seven pieces. That mobility matters most if it helps running back Bucky Irving sustain Tampa Bay’s preferred game script. Irving has 825 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns through nine games, and the Buccaneers have leaned on him heavily during their recent stretch. A Daniels start would put more pressure on the offense to pair designed quarterback movement, play-action and a disciplined rushing attack rather than asking the rookie to win a pass-heavy game from the pocket. – Irving remains the offensive centerpiece, but the Buccaneers have also discussed reducing his workload after he logged 111 carries over the previous five games. Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker could take on more work if Tampa Bay wants to preserve Irving while maintaining its physical identity. – Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs presents the defining test for the defense after reaching 1,000 rushing yards in nine games. Yarcho argued that limiting Gibbs on the ground and as a receiver would give the Buccaneers a better chance to pressure Jared Goff without relying heavily on blitze

away.headline: Buccaneers at Lions: Initial injury report for Week 11
away.blurb: Mayfield (foot/right thumb) was held out of Wednesday’s session after suffering an injury to his foot and ankle area during the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Chicago Bears. The veteran quarterback had reportedly been wearing a walking boot periodically throughout the bye week but was seen without one Wednesday while observing practice in street clothes. Aside from Mayfield, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) was the only other Buccaneer held out of practice Wednesday. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee), who missed Tampa Bay’s game against Chicago, was a limited participant. Cornerback Josh Hayes (knee), tight end Cade Otton (thumb) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) participated fully. Hayes returned to practice Wednesday, opening his 21-day activation window from injured reserve. For Detroit, center Cade Mays (ankle) was the only player listed as a non-participant. Cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip) and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) were among six players listed as limited, while safety Kerby Joseph (knee) was listed as a full participant. The Lions conducted a walkthrough Wednesday, meaning their participation designations were estimates. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

They will look to remain undefeated at Arrowhead Stadium with the Arizona Cardinals coming to town for Kansas City's final home game in a month. These two teams are in completely different positions, as the Cardinals are already playing for draft position after turning to rookie quarterback Carson Beck. The Chiefs are battling for the top overall seed in the AFC and trying to overtake the Broncos in the AFC West . Kansas City unsurprisingly enters this showdown as a massive favorite over the three-win Cardinals. However, what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what its computer model forecasts prior to kickoff. Cardinals at Chiefs: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction Aug 9, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals safety Joey Blount (32) against the Kansas City Chiefs during a preseason NFL game at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 88.0%, Cardinals 11.9%. ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 88.0%, Cardinals 11.9%. With a win probability of nearly 90%, this figure marks the largest advantage the Chiefs have held in the matchup predictor all season, even more than when they played the Dolphins or Jets. Chiefs on SI's Take The Cardinals are in the midst of a putrid offensive stretch in which they've mustered a mere nine points over the last two weeks. They sent Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore at the trade deadline and lost Gardner Minshew II to a torn UCL, forcing them to rely on their third-round rookie to orchestrate the offense. While the Chiefs recently endured a mini-slump that featured losses to the Seahawks and Broncos, they have bounced back by scoring 35 points in consecutive wins. Patrick Mahomes has finally shaken off the early rust coming off his torn ACL and LCL, and this squad is now playing some of its best football all year. Due to the lopsided nature of this particular game, the medical staff is in no rush to get Kenneth Walker III (groin) back on the field. Rookie tailback Emmett Johnson should continue to handle a large offensive workload, which he has undoubtedly earned with 171 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns last week. The Chiefs will face every team from the NFC West this season and have already played Seattle. They still have the Rams and 49ers after this weekend, which will serve as the final interconference matchups on the schedule. All three of Arizona's victories have actually come on the road, so perhaps it will give KC a run for its money. However, the computer model indicates that this one will get out of hand fairly quickly Sunday afternoon. picks.headline: Here’s who national experts predict will win Arizona Cardinals at KC Chiefs game
picks.blurb: Here’s who national experts predict will win Arizona Cardinals at KC Chiefs game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football winners/losers Current wins 1st title Wemby drops 50 ... again Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur paces the sideline during a football game between the Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz., on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. (Ayrton Breckenridge/USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co) Pete Grathoff · Kansas City Star Sat, November 21, 2026 at 6:43 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals franchise history dates to 1920 when the team began play in Chicago. This year's team has a chance to do something unseen in franchise history: Defeat the Chiefs in Kansas City. The Cardinals left Chicago for St. Louis in 1960, the same year the Chiefs began play in the American Football League. In 1988, the Cardinals moved to Arizona. No matter what city the Cardinals have called home, they have never won in Kansas City. The Chiefs hold a 5-0-1 record all-time against the Cardinals, and that tie sounds like it was a barn burner: 6-6 in 1970. The national NFL pundits don't think the Cardinals will get that first win in KC on Sunday. Here is how 67 national experts see things playing out in Sunday's game, which starts at noon and will be broadcast on KCTV (Ch. 5). A 27-13 Chiefs win is the outlook from the Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff, who wrote: "Carson Beck and the Cardinals were embarrassed in a 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10. More embarrassment is coming for Arizona. Kansas City will be too tough at home." A 27-12 Chiefs victory is the call from the Associated Press' Rob Maaddi. Here is an excerpt from his story: "The Cardinals upset the Rams in Los Angeles with Jacoby Brissett and they rallied to beat the Cowboys in Dallas with Gardner Minshew coming off the bench. Patrick Mahomes, with help from several rookies, had a big game in Atlanta." A 31-13 Chiefs win is the prediction from the Sporting News' Bill Bender. This is an excerpt from his story: "The Chiefs are favored by (a) huge spread. The Cardinals were awful in Carson Beck's debut, in which he had 105 passing yards, two interceptions and took five sacks." A 34-10 Chiefs win is the call from NBC Sports' Mike Florio. He wrote: "They're getting the Cardinals at the perfect time. Then again, pretty much any time anyone gets the Cardinals is the perfect time." The Chiefs will win 28-17 , says the Los Angeles Times' Sam Farmer. This is from his story: "Even without Kenneth Walker III, the Chiefs beat Atlanta with ease. The Cardinals hang tough, but they're playing a rookie quarterback making his second start. Winning in Kansas City is a tall order." Picking the Chiefs are four of the five writers at NFL.com: Brooke Cersosimo (46-23 final score), Jeremy Bergman (34-13), Gennaro Filice (34-10), Bobby Kownack (40-20) and Dan Parr (32-10). This is a snippet of what Cersosimo wrote: "The Kansas City offense is the best it's been in quite some time, thanks to a formidable rushing attack, a spry Travis Kelce and the recent addition of slot receiver Josh Downs. Despite injuries impacting several O-linemen and Kenneth Walker III (who missed last week with a hamstring), the good times should continue for Patrick Mahomes and Co. against a Cardinals defense that's allowing nearly 30 points a game." A Chiefs victory is the prediction for the seven CBS Sports writers: Pete Prisco, Jared Dubin, Ryan Wilson, Dave Richard, John Breech, Tyler Sullivan and Jamey Eisenberg. Prisco thinks it'll be a 33-14 final . Here is a bit of what he wrote: "The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout." A Chiefs blowout victory is also the prediction from all six USA Today writers: Jarrett Bell (34-16 final score), Nick Brinkerhoff (27-7), Chris Bumbaca (31-12), Nate Davis (31-13), Andy Kaufman (30-10) and Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz (34-14). The Chiefs are the choice for the 11 ESPN experts: Matt Bowen, Mike Clay, Jeremy Fowler, Moses Moody, Pamela Maldonado, Lindsey Thiry, Dan Graziano, Kalyn Kahler, Benjamin Solak, Jason Reid and Seth Wickersham. A Chiefs' win is the prediction from the eight Sports Illustrated staff members: Albert Breer, Mitch Goldich, Mike Kadlick, Gilberto Manzano, John Pluym, Matt Verderame, Eva Geitheim and Conor Orr. Taking the Chiefs are all 10 Dallas Morning-News experts: Tim Cowlishaw, Joey Hayden, Damon Marx, Newy Scruggs, Abraham Nudelstejer, Calvin Watkins, Kevin Sherrington, Joseph Hoyt, Dana Larson and Craig Miller. Picking the Chiefs are all nine SB Nation writers: James Dator, David Fucillo, Brandon Gowton, Jared Mueller, Matthew Warren, Mark Schofield, Mookie Alexander, R.J. Ochoa and Ricky O'Donnell Taking the Chiefs are the six Athletic writers: Nick Cosmider Austin Mock, Steven Louis Goldstein, Jon Greenberg, Larry Holder and Josh Kendall.

picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football winners/losers Current wins 1st title Wemby drops 50 ... again Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. away.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles Injury Report
away.blurb: Wide receiver DeVonta Smith is good to go for Sunday's game against the Steelers, but Dontayvion Wicks remains out. The Eagles are healthier coming out of the bye week and will welcome the return of wide receiver DeVonta Smith to the lineup on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, the Eagles will be without Smith's positionmate Dontayvion Wicks for the fourth game in a row. Wicks was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury. The team added a foot injury for Wicks on Friday's report. Linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful for Sunday's game after missing the past two practices with an ankle injury. Running back Will Shipley did not practice on Friday due to an illness. He is questionable as he remains on Injured Reserve with a foot injury. He would need to be activated off Injured Reserve to the 53-man roster by 4 PM on Saturday to be eligible to play against the Steelers. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup and start alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. with Baun out and Mondon doubtful. Campbell missed the past two games with hamstring and quad injuries. Defensive back Michael Carter missed three of the last four games with an abdomen injury. Wide receiver Britain Covey was out for the last two games with a knee injury. Cornerback Jonathan Jones is healthy after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. The Steelers listed six players as questionable, including outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who suffered injuries to his hip and ribs last Sunday night in Cincinnati. Herbig did not practice all week. Three of the players who are questionable – guard Gennings Dunker, wide receiver Michael Pittman, and wide receiver Roman Wilson – are on Injured Reserve and, like Shipley for the Eagles, would need to be activated in order to play against Philadelphia. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday after practicing in a limited capacity Wednesday. Smith told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he was back to 100 percent after missing five of the last six games with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Smael Mondon joined fellow linebacker Zack Baun on the sideline Thursday. Mondon was a full participant with an ankle injury on Wednesday, but did not participate in practice Thursday. Mondon stepped in during the Week 9 game against the Giants before the bye week after Baun suffered a back injury and Jihaad Campbell was out with hamstring and quad injuries. Baun has yet to practice this week, while Campbell is on track to return. Running back Will Shipley, practicing for the first time since the Week 5 game in London, was limited for the second straight day. The Eagles would need to activate him off of Injured Reserve to be eligible for Sunday's game. RB Will Shipley and WR Dontayvion Wicks spotted! home.headline: Steelers vs. Eagles Injury Report
home.blurb: Wide receiver DeVonta Smith is good to go for Sunday's game against the Steelers, but Dontayvion Wicks remains out. The Eagles are healthier coming out of the bye week and will welcome the return of wide receiver DeVonta Smith to the lineup on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, the Eagles will be without Smith's positionmate Dontayvion Wicks for the fourth game in a row. Wicks was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury. The team added a foot injury for Wicks on Friday's report. Linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful for Sunday's game after missing the past two practices with an ankle injury. Running back Will Shipley did not practice on Friday due to an illness. He is questionable as he remains on Injured Reserve with a foot injury. He would need to be activated off Injured Reserve to the 53-man roster by 4 PM on Saturday to be eligible to play against the Steelers. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup and start alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. with Baun out and Mondon doubtful. Campbell missed the past two games with hamstring and quad injuries. Defensive back Michael Carter missed three of the last four games with an abdomen injury. Wide receiver Britain Covey was out for the last two games with a knee injury. Cornerback Jonathan Jones is healthy after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. The Steelers listed six players as questionable, including outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who suffered injuries to his hip and ribs last Sunday night in Cincinnati. Herbig did not practice all week. Three of the players who are questionable – guard Gennings Dunker, wide receiver Michael Pittman, and wide receiver Roman Wilson – are on Injured Reserve and, like Shipley for the Eagles, would need to be activated in order to play against Philadelphia. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday after practicing in a limited capacity Wednesday. Smith told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he was back to 100 percent after missing five of the last six games with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Smael Mondon joined fellow linebacker Zack Baun on the sideline Thursday. Mondon was a full participant with an ankle injury on Wednesday, but did not participate in practice Thursday. Mondon stepped in during the Week 9 game against the Giants before the bye week after Baun suffered a back injury and Jihaad Campbell was out with hamstring and quad injuries. Baun has yet to practice this week, while Campbell is on track to return. Running back Will Shipley, practicing for the first time since the Week 5 game in London, was limited for the second straight day. The Eagles would need to activate him off of Injured Reserve to be eligible for Sunday's game. RB Will Shipley and WR Dontayvion Wicks spotted!
