picks.blurb: Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 11 matchup vs. Panthers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football winners/losers Current wins 1st title Wemby drops 50 ... again Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 11 matchup vs. Panthers BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Calais Campbell #93 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he leads a huddle against the Los Angeles Chargers prior to an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Frank Platko · SB Nation Sun, November 22, 2026 at 3:22 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens will face the Carolina Panthers on the road in Week 11, looking to snap a five-game losing streak and keep their slim hopes of a late-season turnaround alive. Here are Baltimore Beatdown's predictions for this contest. At this point, it's difficult to pick the Ravens. They are coming off one of their worst losses in franchise history and haven't had life for weeks. Are the Panthers a great team? No, but if the last five weeks are any indication of what Sunday will be like, the Ravens will again be dominated in the trenches, commit costly pre-snap penalties, and turn the ball over in critical moments. The dismissal of Marlon Humphrey could help the team morale, but at this point, Humphrey really isn't moving the needle too much. Simply put, there are too many issues right now. Do I have any confidence that the Ravens will magically be able to run the ball, protect the quarterback, sack the opposing QB, clean up their pre-snap issues, and not the turn the ball over? No. X-Factor: Mike Green. Green has been a bright spot on an otherwise underwhelming defense all year with last Monday being arguably the best performance of his young career. If Green can continue to stack games like that, the Ravens could have a future star on their team. Although Trey Hendrickson has been getting a lot of flak from the media, he's been getting consistently double-teamed and chipped which has allowed Green to take advantage of 1-on-1 pass rush situations. Score Prediction: Panthers 31, Ravens 24 I'm not sure I will pick the Ravens for the rest of the year the way it looks right now. This Panthers matchup might be the easiest remaining on the schedule but with no Nnamdi Madubuike and a drama-filled week with Marlon Humphrey, it just doesn't fill like the Ravens are in a great spot mentally to go on the road and find a win. The Panthers offense loves the middle of the field, something Jesse Minter's defense leaves available by design. Chuba Hubbard has been breaking tackles this season, something the Ravens struggle with. The Ravens offensive line doesn't seem likely to magically improve. If the Ravens win, its because they suddenly learned how to run into sacks against a bad offensive line and because Jacoby Brissett took advantage of an injured Panthers secondary room, that looks to get some guys back this week. I think this is easy win for the Panthers, the Ravens can't stop Hubbard and the Panthers bleed clock for a fast, low-scoring win. X-Factor: Ja'Kobi Lane. Lane was a favorite target in Brissett's debut as a Ravens, who targeted Lane 11 times against the Chargers. Unfortunately, Lane only brought in three of those targets and had a really bad drop in the redzone. He was also tackled multiple times on plays that weren't flagged for defensive pass interference inexplicably. I don't think the Jacoby-to-Ja'Kobi connection is going away despite the low success rate. Brissett loves to push the ball down the field and Lane's skillset fits that well. A breakout game from Lane could drive a Ravens win and maybe flip momentum for the season. Score Prediction: Panthers 24, Ravens 17 The Baltimore Ravens have lost five straight games, with their last win dating back to October 11th against the Atlanta Falcons. This Sunday, Baltimore faces another NFC South opponent in the division-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5). Despite the Ravens' recent struggles and internal drama surrounding Marlon Humphrey, this adversity could be the catalyst for one final push to save their season. The Ravens have a favorable matchup against Carolina's offensive tackles. Rasheed Walker has surrendered 5 sacks and 38 pressures this season, while rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has allowed 5 sacks and 26 pressures. Defensively, Carolina has been a buzzsaw against the run, ranking 8th in efficiency and 2nd when stacking the box. However, the Panthers rank just 23rd against intermediate passes, an area Baltimore can exploit. Expect Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane to see a similar target share to last week. X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson: Hendrickson has an opportunity to deliver his signature performance as a Raven. Carolina's struggles at both tackle positions, combined with a tight end room that lacks a reliable option to consistently chip him, create an ideal matchup. Expect Hendrickson to capitalize on these one-on-one opportunities and potentially take over the game as a pass rusher. Score Prediction: Ravens 27, Panthers 16 The Ravens' playoff chances could not be slimmer now after a fifth straight loss last week. However, there is still a mathematical possibility of postseason life — which would pretty much evaporate if they lose any of the next few games. The Panthers are a formidable opponent, but certainly beatable. The Ravens will need to take advantage of Carolina's weak offensive line and create positive plays on defense via the pass rush. Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson have advantageous matchups against both of the Panthers' offensive tackles. X-Factor: Roquan Smith. The Panthers have been one of the top passing attacks over the middle of the field this season, which is Bryce Young's biggest strength. Smith's coverage in this area has been up-and-down, and he will need perform better in this game. The Panthers have multiple big targets who can catch in traffic. Smith will be targeted often and needs to avoid getting lost in open space. Also, can Smith step up as one of the veterans the Ravens need to be more of an impact playmaker? Let's see in this game. Score Prediction: Ravens 21, Panthers 20 It's hard to imagine the Ravens beating anybody after giving the Chargers their first win of the season. This defense holding both Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan in check seems like a pipe dream at this point, especially without Nnamdi Madubuike up front. If the offense can finally figure out how to run the ball, then this team will have a legitimate chance, but I will believe they are capable of doing so when I see it. Jacoby Brissett cannot be asked to throw the ball close to 50 times again this week, but with how impossible running the ball has felt at times, he may be asked to shoulder a significant load once again in his second game with the team. That strategy worked out decently well against Los Angeles, but dropping back that many times behind this offensive line is a recipe for disaster over any extended period of time. It is time for Declan Doyle to pull out all the tricks to get Derrick Henry going this Sunday. X-Factor: Travis Jones: Jones had a strong game against the Chargers and the big nose tackle will need to show up again this week for the defense to have a shot at limiting the damage from Hubbard on the ground. Jones will be needed to provide interior pressure as well in the absence of Madubuike. Score Prediction: Panthers 26, Ravens 21

away.headline: NFL fans react to Ravens’ rumored plan for Lamar Jackson’s return after thumb injury
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens believe Lamar Jackson has a chance to return from his broken right thumb for their Week 16 game against the Cleveland Browns on Dec. 27 if his rehab goes smoothly, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week. Lamar Jackson’s Road From Buffalo Toward a Possible Browns Return In a statement the team released that day, head coach Jesse Minter called recovery timelines “challenging to predict” and said, “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Minter added, “We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season.” Graziano’s report hinges on Jackson’s progress in the same way, leaving the Browns game at M&T Bank Stadium a possibility rather than a set date for his return. For another fan, the calendar is the problem, since a return against the Browns would leave Jackson only two more regular-season games after that one. A Dec. 27 return would be near the optimistic end of Jackson’s reported recovery timetable, though the Ravens have emphasized that his progress, rather than a fixed date, will determine when he can play again. The report comes with Baltimore at 4-6, days after a 23-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who had not won a game before Monday night. Despite the prospect of Jackson returning for the final stretch of the regular season, several fans who responded to the report argued that the Ravens should keep him sidelined and focus on having him healthy for 2027. Jackson’s injury came on Baltimore’s first offensive play of the Nov. 1 game at Buffalo, a 36-10 loss, when his throwing hand caught the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau as he threw. On Nov. 13, the Ravens said the thumb was dislocated and broken and that the injury typically carries a recovery of six to 10 weeks. Sources told ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Jackson had undergone surgery the week before. Fans Point to the Baltimore Ravens’ Slide and Jackson’s Long-Term Health “Week 16 is so late. Just shut him down and run it back next year,” the fan wrote. Baltimore’s form has added to the argument. The Ravens sit fourth in the AFC North and have lost five straight games, including the Buffalo game in which Jackson was hurt and both games since. Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore acquired in a trade, started in Jackson’s place in the loss to the Chargers. “It’s already over … just take the rest of the season off,” another fan responded. Jackson’s health is another piece of it. A high ankle sprain had already cost him three games before the thumb injury, and he has played just 14 full quarters this season. A fan pointed to that history: “Yea bro let’s have Lamar play meaningless games in a lost season after 2 major injuries.” Others looked straight ahead to next season. “What’s the point to play him at that point, come back ’27 stronger,” one fan wrote. away.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. home.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. Chargers are listing WR Ladd McConkey as questionable for Monday night’s game at Baltimore while WR Tre Harris is off the injury report. The Chargers have yet to win a game, and McConkey's production has been very minimal since he's constantly been out of the lineup. The No. 1 receiver for L.A. has just 17 catches on 24 targets for 286 yards and one touchdown this season. There are odds to McConkey to score a touchdown (+340) in this primetime matchp. Can he keep it going against a Raiders team that is 31st in the NFL in points allowed and 32nd in yards per play? Oddsmakers seem to think so, but will Denver be able to cover the number? Las Vegas’ inability to run the ball is also a major issue against a Denver secondary that is 11th in the league in EPA/Pass. Coming out of a bye, Sean Payton is 12-6 straight up in his career as a head coach. I expect him and the Broncos to make quick work of the Raiders as they look to jump ahead of Kansas City for the No. 1 spot in the AFC West. The panel sounds even more certain this week, because every straight-up pick in this roundup goes to the Denver Broncos . Where they part ways is the margin. Eight of the 11 predicted scores below have Denver winning by double digits, while ESPN's Seth Walder sees a tight 24-20 finish. The Raiders Wire staff also went 4-0 for Denver, and its average score of 27-15 lines up almost perfectly with the national predictions. ESPN and NFL.com expect a comfortable Denver win Pamela Maldonado and Eric Moody both landed on 27-13 in ESPN's Week 11 guide . ESPN's Football Power Index agrees with them, giving Denver an 86.3% chance to win by an average of 10.9 points. Walder stands alone as the outlier, and his bold prediction has Broncos tight end Evan Engram finding the end zone. Every NFL.com analyst picked Denver as well, with scores ranging from Jeremy Bergman's 23-9 to Gennaro Filice's 34-17. Bobby Kownack went 24-16, and Dan Parr went 27-13, so the group never sees the Raiders cracking 17 points. Brooke Cersosimo, who went 24-15, believes Denver's poise in tight finishes will help it build a lead and then protect it. CBS Sports has two holdouts Over at CBS Sports , the panel sided with Denver 5-2 against the spread, with Jared Dubin and Ryan Wilson as the lone votes for the Raiders. Pete Prisco has the Broncos winning 31-14, and Jordan Dajani went 30-17. Dajani built his case on recent form, since the Broncos have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. He also noted that the Raiders are tied for the league's worst scoring defense at 28.9 points per game, so he believes Denver "could reach 30 points this week." The spread splits Bleacher Report down the middle Picking a winner was a no-brainer for everyone, but the points told a different story at Bleacher Report. Its experts went just 4-3 for Denver against a 9.5-point spread, with Brad Gagnon, Ian Hanford and Brent Sobleski backing the Raiders with the points. Gagnon kept his reasoning short and to the point. "I expect the Broncos to win, but by a single score," Gagnon wrote. Maurice Moton landed on the other side of that split, and the status of Brock Bowers drove his pick. "Without him or a reliable rushing attack, the rookie could have a tough outing against the Broncos," Moton wrote. SI Betting sees it the same way, laying 10 points with Denver on the way to a 27-16 prediction. Its case leans on a Denver defense that ranks among the league's top 13 in EPA per play, yards per play allowed, and success rate. The verdict on the winner is unanimous, and the verdict on the margin is anything but. Whether Denver can turn this into the rout most of these experts expect will decide which half of the room looks smart on Monday. away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . away.blurb: Runyon's call-up is insurance for Brock Bowers, who is questionable with injuries (ankle and quadriceps) after a limited week of practice . Klint Kubiak has said Bowers could play without practicing, so the Raiders are planning for their star without counting on him. Williams addresses the other sore spot, the interior of a defensive line that will take the field Sunday at least one man short. Tonka Hemingway was ruled out with a stinger after missing all three practices, while Folorunso Fatukasi is questionable (toe injury) despite a full Friday session. Two lines on the Las Vegas Raiders ' final injury report led to the team's last roster moves before Sunday's trip to Denver. The Raiders elevated tight end Carter Runyon and defensive tackle Chris Williams from the practice squad Saturday, shoring up the two spots hit hardest this week. If Bowers sits, Runyon becomes the third tight end behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas, who shook off calf and ankle issues to practice fully Friday. The former FCS All-American from Towson got the same call last week against Seattle, playing two offensive snaps and 18 on special teams in his season debut. Saturday's move is his second elevation of 2026, and NFL rules allow a player only three before he must be signed to the active roster. His best run came with the Bears , where he played 31 games over two seasons and recorded three sacks in 2024 . Cleveland elevated him twice in October before releasing him from its practice squad Oct. 20. Both players will revert to the practice squad after the game. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football winners/losers Current wins 1st title Wemby drops 50 ... again Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

Giants game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football winners/losers Current wins 1st title Wemby drops 50 ... again Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates 4 things to know plus a prediction for Jaguars v. Giants game Paul Bretl, Jaguars Wire · Jaguars Wire Sat, November 21, 2026 at 1:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Up next for the Jacksonville Jaguars is another road matchup, this time against the New York Giants . The Jaguars will enter this game at 7-2, while the Giants are 5-3-1. The last time these two met was in 2022 , and a lot has changed for both teams since then. So for some insight into this current Giants team, Dan Benton of Giants Wire answered a handful of our questions about Sunday's game. How has the addition of JJ McCarthy impacted the Giants' offense? Giants Wire: McCarthy's presence has actually had a significant impact. Matt Nagy had designed the Giants' offense specifically around Jaxson Dart's abilities and when he was lost for the season, they were forced to trim their playbook by up to 50 percent to accommodate Jameis Winston. With McCarthy under center, Nagy was able to restore that 50 percent and run the offense the way he designed it initially. What is the strength of this Giants team this season? Giants Wire: It has been their secondary, without question. Although they have a rotation at safety, the cornerbacks have been able to win one-on-one matchups with impressive frequency. Deonte Banks has gone from an all-time Giants bust into their CB1, and deservedly so. Greg Newsome, who Jaguars fans know all too well, has also played much better than anticipated, earning a contract extension. On the flip side, where have they struggled? Giants Wire: The interior offensive line has been especially poor when it comes to run blocking. They're easily beaten — often embarrassingly so — and it has stymied the running game that was built on power and inside runs. Defensively, while they generate considerable pressure, they've been unable to close and their sack numbers are way down. Then there's the obvious: Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada's struggles from the right hash (hasn't made a single field goal from said hash). Who is an under-the-radar player to know? Giants Wire: Normally, I would have said Banks, but I feel like he's earned his way back onto everyone's radar. Rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields is beginning to emerge and has all but secured the WR2 role, and has become McCarthy's clutch third option behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely, who is having a career season. Fields has yet to drop a pass this season and both his target share and production have steadily increased. Prediction: Who wins and why? Giants Wire: I am predicting an upset. Call it lifelong recognition that the Giants will sometimes play either up or down to the level of the competition. They played down to the competition and lost in Week 10, and will play up to the competition on Sunday in the rain at MetLife Stadium, balancing things back out with a game against the Colts looming. There's no rhyme or reason that this happens, but it's what I'll call an odd Giants tradition. Giants 31, Jaguars 30. home.blurb: The Jaguars dropped their initial injury report for week 11. Center Robert Hainsey was a non-participant. This doesn't come as a surprise when you take into account that head coach Liam Coen had already stated that the veteran hog molly won't be available against New York. With Hainsey expected to sit out the Giants game, Jonah Monheim will get the starting nod at center. It will be the first time the former USC Trojan starts a game this season. On the other hand, running back Bhayshul Tuten popped up on the injury report. He has been dealing with ankle and foot injuries. Mia O'Brien of ESPN Radio noted on Twitter that the sophomore out of Virginia Tech showed up to practice without his helmet . Apart from Tuten, safety Antonio Johnson (ankle), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle), defensive tackle Matt Dickerson (neck), running back Chris Rodriguez (hand), linebacker Jalen McLeod (groin), defensive end Travon Walker (rib), defensive end Danny Striggow (concussion), and Monheim (ankle) were listed as limited participants. Robert Hainsey is questionable for Jaguars vs. Titans, Bhayshul Tuten good to go The Jacksonville Jaguars are 7-2 for the first time since 1999 after winning three games in a row. While nobody will deny that they have dominated, the teams the Jags defeated weren't very good. That will change in Week 11, when they face the New York Giants. The G-Men aren't necessarily a juggernaut, but at 5-3-1, they're nothing to scoff at. They currently lead the NFC East and are the kind of club Jacksonville cannot afford to take lightly. Compounding the issue is that the Jaguars' injury report for Week 11 is quite long. Robert Hainsey and Arik Armstead didn't practice Wednesday Hainsey was dealing with a concussion but cleared protocol ahead of the AFC Showdown against the Tennessee Titans. He started the game but left with a knee injury. Although the injury isn't season-ending, he'll be week-to-week , according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. Aside from Hainsey, defensive tackle Arik Armstead didn't participate, but it was due to personal reasons. He should be back either Thursday or Friday. Tuten hasn't missed a game in spite of the injuries. He toted the rock a season-high 26 times for 88 yards against Tennessee. He'll probably miss Thursday's practice again to keep recovering. The good news is that sophomore defensive end B.J. Green II (elbow) was a full-participant. You may also like: Liam Coen's success makes the latest NY Jets revelation even more puzzling B.J. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Even if you’re not a fan of the Vikings or 49ers, Sunday night’s primetime match in Mexico City is the definition of a “must-watch.” Two of the best teams in the NFL colliding on the international stage, with playoff seeding and bragging rights on the line, is everything the NFL dreamed of when it set the 2026 schedule last spring. The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment. Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte. 1. Vikings' defense slows down 49ers' attack The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game. Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to. The Minnesota Vikings defense ranks 1st in dropback success rate allowed, per @SumerSports The San Francisco 49ers offense ranks 1st in dropback success rate and has the highest dropback success rate of any team through 10 weeks since the 2018 Saints The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready. Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points. 2. Jauan Jennings finds the end zone The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped. Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine . Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night. 3. Sunday's matchup is only the beginning of what's to come This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting? In fact, if both teams continue on their current paths, a late-round playoff matchup may be an inevitable sequel. We simulated the rest of the season using PFN’s NFL Playoff Predictor. 🔮 Here’s the projected playoff bracket 👀 pic.twitter.com/QBo8zogNJ6 There’s a lot of football to be played, and neither team is in the easiest of divisions, but these are two squads built for postseason success. You may need to bookmark this one, but I predict that Sunday will not be the last time we see Minnesota and San Francisco battle this year. Whoever takes round two may end up having Valentine’s Day plans at SoFi Stadium. picks.blurb: Sportsbook Insiders: Insights on Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for Sunday Night Football; Kirk Cousins Impact Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins has transformed the NFC playoff picture since being traded from Las Vegas to Minnesota at the trade deadline, and that’s set up a very interesting Sunday Night Football matchup in Week 11. The Vikings are set to face the San Francisco 49ers in a neutral site game in Mexico City, and there are a ton of playoff implications at stake. Not only are the Vikings battling for first place in the NFC North, but a win over San Fran would give Minnesota a legit shot at the No. 1 seed in the conference. A Cousins trade materialized for Minnesota after back-to-back losses to Detroit and Buffalo where Kyler Murray (against Detroit) and Carson Wentz (against Buffalo) showed that they simply aren’t playing quarterback at a high enough level for the Vikings to win a Super Bowl. That sentiment has changed in the futures market, as the Vikings are now priced around 15/1 to win it all after an upset win over Green Bay in Week 10. The odds for that game shifted in a big way after Cousins was acquired, as the same goes for Week 11 against San Francisco. Sports Illustrated spoke to several oddsmakers this week to see just how much the Cousins’ acquisition has changed the Vikings’ outlook in this Sunday Night matchup. How Much Kirk Cousins Impacts Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for NFL Week 11 The Vikings opened as 3.5-point underdogs in Week 11 after their win over Green Bay, but that line has continued to move towards the Vikings, settling at 3. While that’s a minor move, there’s a chance this line would have been set as far as 49ers -7 if Murray or Wentz was under center on Sunday night. “Well, if the quarterback play continued to go the way it was before Cousins arrived, the Vikings would have been close to a touchdown underdog, rather than a field goal underdog,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. That’s at least a four-point swing in favor of the 49ers, though not every book had that price. BetMGM and FanDuel both told Sports Illustrated that the spread would likely be close to four or five. “Not too much believe it or not, probably was about a point or so move,” Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated. The reason being is there isn't a major gap between Cousins and Murray. The main reason for this spread being close is the strength of the defense. Both QBs are capable, it helps Minnesota's future odds more because if one gets injured they have a capable backup to come in.” It’s interesting to hear about different pricing across the industry, as Fanatics has a much different grade – but similar to DraftKings – when it comes to the Murray vs. Cousins debate: “We opened up a lookahead line on the day of trade deadline day, it was plus seven,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “And now the Vikings are three-point dogs, just to give you an idea of how highly we rate Kirk Cousins versus Murray or Wentz.” In his first start with the Vikings, Cousins threw for 207 yards, two scores and one pick, and he has 22 touchdown passes in the 2026 season. There’s no doubt that this Vikings team – which has the No. 2 defense in EPA/Play in 2026 – has a much better chance of competing with San Fran’s No. 1 offense with Cousins calling the shots. What Would the Vikings vs. 49ers Spread Be in San Francisco? This game is also unusual because of the neutral site aspect. While this is technically a home game for San Francisco, it likely would be favored by more Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara. Still, Avello explained that home field doesn’t matter as much as it used to when DraftKings sets the spread for games. “ The Niners playing at home – there's a misconception with home-field advantage,” Avello said. When you look at it across the league, it's only a couple of points. Some teams get a little stronger, and a lot of it has to do with weather. So, the Niners would have been only maybe another point and a half at home, so maybe the line would have been 4.5.” San Francisco is a perfect 5-0 at home in the 2026 season, so it’ll be interesting to see if Kyle Shanahan’s team can hold up on a neutral field. The 49ers (8-1) are looking to maintain their lead in the NFC and NFC West, but a loss to Minnesota would bring it back down into the same playing field with other two-loss teams like Chicago and Detroit. away.blurb: Many fans will no doubt view Sunday's matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings as marking the NFL's return to Mexico . "I fell in love with the 49ers in the mid-80s because of Joe Montana. I've attended every game held in Mexico, and it's great that they're back," said Octavio Zúñiga, a 50-year-old fan. "Last time (in 2022), they came out carrying the Mexican flag as they entered the stadium. That commitment to the Mexican fan base is truly appreciated." November 19, 2026 / 8:39 AM CST / CBS Minnesota The reality is, the league never truly left. Although Mexico last hosted a regular-season game in 2022, the league's growth in the country has been steady, according to Arturo Olivé, managing director of NFL Mexico. Over the past 18 years, the league's domestic fan base has surged from roughly 10 million to 40 million, according to the NFL. "We have grown significantly over these years thanks to the constant, continuous, daily work of our team," Olivé said. "Eighteen years ago, we chose our battles and focused our attention on the specific areas we needed to improve in order to expand our fan base." In Mexico, the NFL trails only soccer — the national sport — in total fans. The game's popularity is no coincidence; American football is as much a part of Mexican sports tradition as soccer, boxing, and lucha libre. The Mexico game will be the last of the nine international NFL games played this season, a league record. To expand its reach, NFL Mexico invested heavily in flag football, which has steadily gained traction and now boasts roughly 4 million players nationwide. While impressive, Olivé acknowledges that in a nation of more than 130 million people, there is still vast room for growth. To accelerate adoption, the league signed an agreement with the National Commission of Physical Culture and Sport (CONADE) to expand the sport across public schools. "With 4 million children in the program, we are barely scratching the surface. Forty million fans in Mexico is a lot, but there are still another 80 or 90 million people we could reach," Olivé said. CONADE, the agency that oversees Mexico's federal sports budget, is eager to promote flag football ahead of its debut as an Olympic sport at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Mexico's women's national team has already secured an Olympic berth. "We believe this alliance turns schools into spaces for participation, well-being and talent development," said Rommel Pacheco, general director of CONADE. "We want more girls, boys, and young people to play an accessible and inclusive sport." home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray are out as expected, while just Jay Ward and Isaiah Rodgers are listed as questionable. Kevin O’Connell said that Rodgers felt good in Friday’s practice but was limited, and they will see how he feels after practice and with post-practice treatment. More likely both play than not play on Sunday night. For the 49ers, a bunch of players with questionable designations. The biggest two are WR Mike Evans and LB Dre Greenlaw. Evans has been limited all week and listed as questionable, but with Achilles tendonitis I would think they’d want to see how he does with a full speed practice before having him start on Sunday night at altitude. We’ll see. Kyle Shanahan says they’ll see how he does in a Saturday walk-through before deciding on whether he’ll play on Sunday night or not. Dre Greenlaw is dealing with a neck injury and his been limited in the last two practices after missing the first one this week. Kyle Shanahan said that neck/nerve injuries can be difficult to predict, but he’s heading in the right direction. That’s another one that while questionable (which means more likely to play in reality) may be closer to a 50/50 chance. He would be a significant loss if he couldn’t go on Sunday night. Upton Stout is their slot corner and has been limited all week with shoulder/neck injuries and is also questionable. This is reportedly an AC joint issue that he has been playing through since he suffered it early in October so it would seem more likely he continue to play through it on Sunday night, although it has affected his performance. As they prepare to visit the Washington Commanders this Monday night, one of the most intriguing storylines on the NFL Week 11 slate is whether Cincinnati can maintain this historic pace. Before we break down the matchup and the odds on the board, be sure to use our Polymarket promo code and download the Action Network app to get the best trading insights across sports, politics, and entertainment. Bengals vs. Commanders: Polymarket Odds Cincinnati enters this Monday night matchup as 6.5-point favorites with a 73% implied probability on the moneyline. The consensus total sits at 54.5, meaning traders are effectively projecting a 30.5-point team total for the Bengals. This market has experienced significant line movement over the past week. When Cincinnati secured its fifth consecutive game scoring 30 or more points, their odds spiked. They went from trading at a 64% implied probability on Nov. 14 to their current 73% standing. There are several player props worth monitoring that correlate directly with this 30-point scoring pace. At the top of the board is the performance of quarterback Joe Burrow. His Over/Under totals for completions, passing yards, and interceptions are critical data points. Without another elite showing from Burrow under center, it is highly unlikely the Bengals clear that high-scoring threshold again. The same logic applies to anytime touchdown markets for his primary targets, Ja'Marr Chase and Mike Gesicki, who have already hauled in seven and six receiving touchdowns this season, respectively. Joe Burrow Has the Bengals Offense Operating at an Elite Level Without question, Joe Burrow is the centerpiece of the Bengals' offense. So far, the quarterback has been absolutely lethal, cementing his position as a frontrunner for the regular-season MVP award. Burrow’s elite firepower was on full display in the 38-18 blowout victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers. The quarterback was flawless, completing 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns without a single interception. With Ja'Marr Chase hauling in 231 receiving yards, the Bengals now look like an unstoppable juggernaut looking to extend its streak this Monday night. While this is the first run of its kind in franchise history, the team is not content with simply writing themselves into the record books. The Bengals have their sights set on a deep playoff run. Is a Taylor Swift tour coming ? Here’s what the odds say. Can the Commanders’ Defense End the Bengals' 30-Point Streak? To stall Cincinnati’s offense, Washington's pass rush must collapse the pocket and disrupt Burrow's timing before he can find Ja'Marr Chase downfield. However, traders remain highly skeptical. The Commanders' defensive backfield has shown a tendency to surrender explosive plays, making them a prime target for the Bengals. To make matters even worse, Washington has already surrendered 30 or more points to multiple opponents this season, including the Cowboys, Colts, and Seahawks. Ultimately, this matchup comes down to pressure versus precision. If Washington fails to generate a relentless pass rush, Burrow will pick their secondary apart, making it highly probable that the Bengals clear the 30-point threshold for a sixth consecutive week. Longest 30-Point Streaks in the NFL and Bengals Schedule While the Bengals have been absolutely lethal, they are still far from the all-time NFL record. That honor belongs to the St. Louis Rams, who hung at least 30 points on the board in 14 consecutive games. Their historic run began late in 1999, the year they won the Super Bowl, and stretched through the first half of the 2000 campaign. Another incredible, and much more recent, streak belongs to the San Francisco 49ers, who reached the 30-point mark in nine straight games across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. If Cincinnati manages to clear the 30-point threshold again against the Commanders, prediction markets’ focus will immediately shift toward projecting this streak down the stretch. As the Bengals navigate the back half of the 2026 season, their remaining strength of schedule presents several tests. That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn't even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now they are taking their show on the road to play the Washington Commanders in their house on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow is 0-2 so far in his career against the Commanders, but that comes with some pretty big caveats. The first loss was the game in which he injured his knee midway through the game as a rookie. The other loss came in an absolute monster of a shootout where the Bengals defense did not stop the Commanders or Jayden Daniels a single time in 2024, with the game ending 38-33. That would not be the first time Burrow would helm a losing team despite putting up more than 30 points over the next few seasons. These teams are drastically different as the Cincinnati defense has had a major overhaul, and Washington is far from the team it was during Daniels' rookie season. There is no doubt Daniels is a talented quarterback, but the Commanders themselves seem to be a very average to below-average team that needs a combination of home run hits on offense and a handful of turnovers to spark a win. Meanwhile, Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are giving their best impressions of the Colts' offense during Peyton Manning's heyday by trusting their quarterback to put up points with his top weapons over a balanced attack. That has led to four straight games of four touchdowns for Burrow, which ties a record set by Manning. The real x-factor here will be the Bengals defense. Will the version we have seen since the Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons show up that has been able to contain opposing offenses that tried to test their linebackers and safeties? Or will the young players at those positions allow a few too many big plays? Here is how the oddsmakers and experts feel about the game. The Bengals are currently 6.5-point road favorites against the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It really is a fairly big deal when a road team gets almost a touchdown advantage over a home team. It clearly shows that there is a step between where these two teams are currently at. The point total is set at 53.5 is the second highest of the week. That is fair because even when this team has faced teams like the Tennessee Titans, they have given up opportunities to score. 10 of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com's experts are expecting the Bengals to extend their win streak to six games NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick I think this team has really turned a corner as far as this defense is concerned. The young linebacker duo of Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter have grown enough to prove to be a competent — maybe not the most consistent — duo. That is the level of play this defense needs when the defensive line led by Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence is able to get penetration. We will have to see how well they contain Daniels, who can really cause some damage by extending plays with his legs. All of that more or less will determine how much the Commanders lose by. Washington has no way of slowing down or throwing off this offense. The Bengals are getting into at least the 30s. Can the Commanders keep pace? Final Score: Bengals 45, Commanders 25 Who Dey! away.blurb: The Washington Commanders got some bad news at the end of Friday’s practice. Starting cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the last day of practice. He did not practice on Saturday and the Commanders listed him as questionable on the final injury report for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . Losing Robertson would be significant. He’s been Washington’s best and most consistent defensive back. His competitiveness sets the tone for the entire team. I’ll monitor over the next, you know, 48 hours,” Quinn said. In some good news, no players were ruled out for Monday night’s game. However, three others were listed as questionable: Croskey-Merritt had his 21-day window opened last week. Quinn indicated on Saturday that things were trending positively for Washington’s starting running back to return on Monday. White has handled the bulk of running back duties while Croskey-Merritt is out, but Quinn seemed to indicate that he believed White could play against the Bengals. Finally, Patrick is listed as questionable, but practiced fully on Saturday and Quinn said he'd be back in the starting lineup. He suffered a concussion two weeks ago against the Rams and missed last week’s win over the Giants . Former starter Nick Allegretti played well in Patrick’s absence. away.headline: Bengals reveal 2 new injury designations hours before Week 10 vs. Steelers
away.blurb: At approximately 11:30 a.m. ET, the Bengals announced that starting right guard Dalton Risner and backup offensive tackle Myles Hinton were both questionable to play against the Steelers with illnesses. Bengals reveal 2 new injury designations hours before Week 10 vs. Steelers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Bengals reveal 2 new injury designations hours before Week 10 vs. Steelers Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Sun, November 15, 2026 at 10:41 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Less than 10 hours before kickoff, the Cincinnati Bengals announced two new injury designations for their Week 10 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. Risner, who was drafted by the Denver Broncos in the second round of the 2019 NFL Draft before joining the Bengals in 2025, has played a big part in keeping Joe Burrow protected in 2026, appearing in eight games, with Pro Football Focus crediting him with three sacks allowed in their October 29 update. If Risner can't suit up, expect Jacob Bayer or Jalen Rivers to slot in as the starting right guard for Sunday Night Football. home.headline: Commanders injury updates: Four questionable vs Bengals on Monday
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders got some bad news at the end of Friday’s practice. Starting cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the last day of practice. He did not practice on Saturday and the Commanders listed him as questionable on the final injury report for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . Losing Robertson would be significant. He’s been Washington’s best and most consistent defensive back. His competitiveness sets the tone for the entire team. According to head coach Dan Quinn, Robertson could be a game-time decision on Monday. “So, yeah, [Amik’s injury] on the last play of the day [Friday], so it was sore today, so we held [him] out. I’ll monitor over the next, you know, 48 hours,” Quinn said. In some good news, no players were ruled out for Monday night’s game. However, three others were listed as questionable: Croskey-Merritt had his 21-day window opened last week. Quinn indicated on Saturday that things were trending positively for Washington’s starting running back to return on Monday. White has handled the bulk of running back duties while Croskey-Merritt is out, but Quinn seemed to indicate that he believed White could play against the Bengals. Finally, Patrick is listed as questionable, but practiced fully on Saturday and Quinn said he'd be back in the starting lineup. He suffered a concussion two weeks ago against the Rams and missed last week’s win over the Giants . Former starter Nick Allegretti played well in Patrick’s absence. home.headline: Bengals Injury Report: Joe Burrow, Dalton Risner on Opening Commanders Injury List
home.blurb: The opening injury report for Commanders Week just dropped from the Bengals . Guard Dalton Risner (knees) did not practice, as fans hope to see him get a session in over the next two days. Joe Burrow was a full participant with his illness so that should quell any fear he may miss Monday's game. Dax Hill is also dealing with an illness. Dylan Fairchild (oblique) logged a limited showing after his injury on Sunday night. Outside of those names, there aren't many big ones to discuss. Cincinnati should get back Andrei Iosivas, Brian Parker and Jalen Davis this week after all three logged full Thursday sessions. Backup safety Kyle Dugger (quad) logged a limited session as a nice sign of improvement. A few other special-team names popped up with illnesses but what looks like a big injury list should end up thinning out across the next few days. "Yeah. Those guys have been so good, and I love playing with them," Burrow said about Drew Sample and Chase Brown. "They take it very seriously, and they want to win. They want to be great, and they put so much mental energy into working throughout the week to understand the guys they're going against. To understand what their pass rush moves are and all the different front looks that we can see. I know that they're not satisfied either, but those guys are lights out." "We've already had all the confidence in the world," Burrow said on Sunday about the team's execution and improvement following a 2-2 start. "This happened on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday practices, and the rest took care of itself on Sunday. I think we all had a good feeling about what was going to happen today, and we went out and made it happen ... We just kept getting better — just grinding at practice and improving, (and) improving through meetings. We've got great coaches that make adjustments and try to put us in really good positions to go and make plays, and right now we are." On Thursday, head coach Zac Taylor met with the media and provided several injury updates. The most notable was wide receiver Tee Higgins, who battled some minor issues during Sunday’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, but it wasn’t believed to be significant. Taylor said Thursday that Higgins is good to go this week, so it sounds like he won’t miss any practice time.
